title: Clarify per-invocation metering & quota attribution for embeddings/rerank with synchronous tool-calls and structured outputs
creator: Aisha Kumar
description:
Summary:
We have recurring discrepancies in customer billing and quota enforcement for non-chat endpoints that do embeddings or rerank, especially when the request flow performs synchronous tool-calls or returns structured output. Examples we observed: duplicated token counts when a reranker calls a model internally for scoring, charges for internal tool-call metadata, and incorrect quota decrements when a single user request fans out to multiple internal operations.

Problem details and motivation:
- Endpoints affected: /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank (non-chat variants), and structured-output flows that trigger synchronous tool-calls.
- Incorrect behaviors we've seen:
  * A single API call to rerank leads to N model scoring invocations; current metering sometimes attributes all token usage to the customer multiple times, inflating bill and exhausting quotas.
  * Tool-calls executed synchronously as part of a structured output pipeline are sometimes billed as separate external invocations rather than internal execution steps, causing rate-limit surprises.
  * Rerank/embeddings semantics (per-candidate scoring vs. aggregate embedding generation) are inconsistently reflected in the usage ledger, making downstream usage analytics and cost reports noisy.

Goals:
1) Define a clear per-invocation metering model for non-chat endpoints that:
   - attributes cost to the original API request (one line item) while preserving granular breakdowns (model input/output tokens, rerank candidate multipliers, tool-call CPU/GPU time) in our analytics pipeline;
   - prevents double-counting when internal helper calls are made to the same model;
   - enforces quotas using request-level gating so that a fan-out doesn’t allow bypassing per-minute/per-day quotas.
2) Implement the metering changes with minimal latency overhead and full auditability for customer disputes.

Proposed design (high-level):
- Metering abstraction: introduce a request-level invocation ID (req_invocation_id) that is generated at API gateway time for every incoming API call. All downstream internal operations (model scoring, embedding generation, tool-call orchestration) must include this ID when emitting usage events. Billing job will deduplicate by (req_invocation_id, operation_type) according to defined aggregation rules.
- Aggregation rules:
  * Model tokens: charge input + output tokens once per logical request. If internal scoring reuses cached KV state or shares the same model invocation, treat as same token bank.
  * Rerank: represent as base request cost + candidate_cost * num_candidates. Candidate_cost is an agreed embedding/rerank unit (see acceptance criteria).
  * Tool-calls: classify synchronous tool-calls spawned by the request as "internal helper" and include their compute cost in the original request line item rather than as separate API invocations. External integrations called directly by the user (e.g., webhooks to customer endpoints) remain billed as separate external operations.
- Quotas and rate limits: enforce at request-invocation granularity. When a request would fan out, check the quota before allowing launch; if quota insufficient, return a 429 with a clear reason and a metering snapshot.
- Audit and evidence: attach per-request metering digest to long-term logs (S3) with req_invocation_id, aggregated token counts, and component breakdowns to assist reconciliation.

Acceptance criteria:
- Billing pipeline deduplicates previously duplicated charges for at least 95% of historical offending requests in a replay dataset.
- Quota enforcement prevents overrun for fan-out request test cases in synthetic load tests.
- New request-level billing line appears in billing UI and CSV export with both aggregated cost and component breakdown.
- Customer dispute workflow can retrieve a per-request metering digest within 48 hours.

Implementation plan (phases):
1) Instrumentation (week 1) — API gateway generates req_invocation_id, propagate through service mesh. Add usage event field req_invocation_id to our usage_event schema. Backfill shim in older services for a short period.
2) Aggregation & billing logic change (week 2) — implement dedupe and aggregation rules in billing worker, add rerank candidate multiplier config.
3) Quota enforcement (week 2–3) — add request-level quota checks and 429 behavior.
4) Testing & rollout (week 3) — replay historical logs, run canary on small subset of traffic, add dashboards and alerts.
5) Full rollout and reconciliation (week 4) — monitor billing deltas and customer complaints, provide opt-in dispute fast-path.

Testing plan and metrics:
- Create a replay dataset from last 30 days focusing on high-fanout rerank and embedding calls (dataset stored in s3://redwood-billing-replay/eng-10742). Compare charges before/after change.
- Success metrics: 95% reduction in duplicate line items; reject rate for legitimate requests remains <0.1% extra; discrepancy rate in accounting ledger for customers using affected endpoints drops by 90%.

Rollout and mitigation strategy:
- Canary 1: 1% of traffic, only non-paying test orgs. Monitor billing diff and error rates.
- Canary 2: 10% of traffic with billing notifications enabled for alpha customers.
- Full rollout with a 24-hour pause and rollback option if billing delta > 5% or error rate spikes > 0.5%.

Open design decisions and trade-offs:
- Deduplication semantics: whether to dedupe by req_invocation_id only or by (req_invocation_id, model_variant). Dedupe-by-request is simpler but may hide legitimate multi-model charges. Proposal: dedupe-by-request for same model_variant; allow separate charges for different model_variants.
- Tool-call classification: treat all sync tool-calls as internal vs. only those marked internal by service metadata. We propose the latter to avoid changing semantics for webhook-based tool integrations.

Out-of-scope for this ticket:
- Long-term product-level pricing changes for rerank (that would require PM/legal). This ticket only changes metering and attribution.

Long-term follow-ups (captured as separate tickets):
- PM work to formalize candidate_cost pricing and publish docs.
- SDK changes to surface per-request metering digest to customers in responses.
